sentences.text: Learned counsel for petitioner submits that petitioner is owner of land bearing No.177/4 measuring 0.90 acres and 177/7 measuring 0.78 acres of the land sitauted at village - Kadar.
Though the land of petitioner was acquired, however, the proper amount of compensation has not been calculated and in the award less amount of compensation was calculated and mentioned therein.
Award was passed on 02.11.2017, petitioner immediately thereafter submitted an application before the respondent No.4 raising his grievance on 18.07.2018.
Respondent No.4 has not given any heed to the representation/objection raised by petitioner and therefore, the writ petition is filed.

He also pointed out that in the same time, petitioner has also submitted an application before Tahsildar and based on the application submitted, Tahsildar directed for spot inspection, and Panchanama was prepared by Patwari mentioning that land of petitioner bearing Kh. No. 177/7 area 0.78 acres was acquired.
3.
Learned State counsel for intervener submits that the land acquisition proceedings initiated by respondent No.4 is on their request.
The land which is sought to be acquired was notified, and after conclusion of proceedings award was passed by Sub- Divisional Officer (Revenue).

He also submits that if petitioner is having grievance with regard to quantum of amount of compensation, petitioner is having remedy under Section 3.G (5) of Act of 1956 to submit an application before the Arbitrator and petitioner can very well raise his grievance before the Arbitrator.
He submits that within the State of Chhattisgarh, concerned Additional Commissioner having territorial jurisdiction is nominated as Arbitrator.
4. I have heard learned counsel for parties and perused the documents placed on record.
5. Grievance of petitioner is with regard to quantum of compensation based on the area of land which was alleged to have been acquired by interveners for the purpose of construction of road.
Land acquisition is undisputedly under the provisions of National Highway Act 1956 (In short "the Act of 1956").
The notification of acquisition is also under Section 3.

Section 3G (5) of the Act of 1956 deals with the grievance with regard to the determination of the amount of compensation to be raised before the Arbitrator by any of the parties i.e. acquiring authority or the land oustees.
As petitioner has not filed any application under Section 3G(5) of the Act of 1956 but has submitted an application before the Land Acquisition Officer on 18.07.2018 raising his grievance.

6. In the aforementioned facts of the case without entering into the merits of the claim of petitioner,
this petition is disposed off at this stage permitting petitioner to submit appropriate application before Arbitrator appointed/nominated by the Central Government for dealing with the issue and if such application is submitted, the Arbitrator shall consider and decide the application in accordance with law expeditiously preferably within a period of six months from the date of receipt of application.
7. With the aforesaid observations and directions, this petition stands disposed off.
